Text: Humana is positioned for a significant earnings recovery following improvements in its 2027 Medicare Advantage Star Ratings, according to Evercore analyst Elizabeth Anderson. Humana recorded broad improvements across multiple contracts, including its key H5216 contract, which achieved 4-star summary ratings for both Medicare Part C and Part D. Of 13 contracts, four gained a star while one lost a star. Text: $UNH Part 1 Following UnitedHealth Group’s (UNH) third quarter 2026 earnings conference call, the remaining capacity under their share repurchase program is tracked across two metrics: management's annual dollar guidance and the board's authorized share facility. 1. Full-Year Target: Management previously raised its 2026 full-year repurchase target to "at least $5.0 billion" (up from an initial $2.5 billion). Remaining for 2026: Because UNH reached the $5.0 billion mark by the end of Q3, there is no formal remaining dollar commitment left on their minimum target for the year. Text: $UNH Part 2 2. Text: $UNH part 1 The post-midterm bullish case for UnitedHealth Group (UNH) centers on legislative gridlock and the removal of election-related policy overhang. Historically, managed care organizations face sentiment pressure leading up to midterms over potential regulatory crackdowns, drug pricing reform, or aggressive scrutiny of Medicare Advantage. With the election establishing a divided government, the likelihood of sweeping, disruptive healthcare legislation or radical structural overhauls to pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) drops substantially. This policy gridlock provides clear regulatory visibility, allowing investors to refocus on UnitedHealth’s fundamental earnings power rather than worst-case legislative outcomes.

Author: newtwo99
Text: $UNH part 2 Beyond policy stability, UNH offers an appealing combination of defensive resilience, valuation support, and dual-engine growth across its Optum services and UnitedHealthcare insurance segments. In an environment where macroeconomic and market volatility remain elevated, UnitedHealth generates robust, non-cyclical cash flows and maintains strong capital returns, recently bolstered by share buyback authorizations and steady dividend growth. With the stock trading at a discount relative to historical multiples following pre-election uncertainty, the clearing of political event risk provides a favorable entry point for multiple expansion as steady Medicare, commercial, and value-based care enrollment drive compounding earnings growth.
